thread:
Maya: heads up — we've got a cluster of failed batch inferences starting ~08:12 UTC. looks correlated with some cross-region failover traffic.
Jamal: which region? any error codes from the jobs?
Maya: majority from us-west1 -> attempts falling back to eu-west1. failures are GPU allocation timeouts + a bunch of 503s from the inference frontends. sample log: 
```
2026-03-18T08:12:23Z job-id=btch-143 status=error reason=runtime_alloc_timeout region=eu-west1
2026-03-18T08:12:25Z frontend=gen-01 err=upstream_503 conn_id=7
```
Wei: oh — that sounds like our geo-fallback sent traffic to eu-west1 but eu had a maintenance window and GPU pools were cordoned.
Lucas: confirmed — eu-west1 had a rolling drain for firmware update, resize job queued. Dedicated GPU capacity currently at 12% available.
Sara: why did traffic even go to eu? I thought we pin long-running batch to region=us-west by default.
Maya: routing policy is latency_steering with fallback=nearest and geo-dns TTL=60s. when us-west1 SNAT pool started saturating, health probes started failing and regional weight shifted.
Jamal: SNAT exhaustion? any NAT gateway alarms?
infra-bot: alarm: nat/snat-port-usage/us-west1 > 95% (08:09 UTC)
oncall-bot: page: @oncall.rotation — high NAT port usage us-west1 causing region egress failure
Wei: that explains it. when SNAT ports exhausted, connections to model registry + scheduler timed out -> frontends marked unhealthy -> GeoDNS relocated traffic.
Lucas: but geo-dns should respect region pinning for jobs flagged as location_sensitive. Did the batch jobs lose their pin?
Maya: they were launched with location_sensitive=true but the pin cache is routeable only for live sessions. These are non-interactive batch tasks created via the batch API; they use the normal geo steering.
Sara: the result is eu-west1 got a sudden spike of egress and compute requests while it was mid-maintenance. We paid cross-region egress + preempted capacity, and ~40 jobs failed.
Jamal: list of immediate mitigations?
Maya: short list: 1) revert geo-dns fallback to prefer origin region while SNAT errors persist (set fallback_policy=origin-prefer for 1h) 2) increase SNAT ephemeral ports in us-west1 (add SNAT nodes) 3) temporarily pin batch job creation to reserved dedicated pool in us-west1 4) lower GeoDNS TTL to 10s for faster steering corrections
Wei: + add a temporary static NAT pool for heavy egress jobs (customers using large embeddings).
Lucas: done: altered routing policy to origin-prefer and reduced TTL to 10s. Pushed with infra flag: 
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/route-config -d '{"region":"us-west1","fallback_policy":"origin-prefer","geodns_ttl":10}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
infra-bot: deploy started: route-config v2026.03.18.1
deploy-bot: canary routing change deployed to control-plane-2 (08:27 UTC)
Maya: I'm requeueing the failed jobs to the reserved us-west1 pool now. Will monitor.
Sara: cost note — cross-region egress to eu-west1 for 40 failed jobs ~ estimated $1.2k due to large model downloads. We should include this in postmortem.
Jamal: follow-ups: *increase SNAT capacity long-term* (we need autoscaling on NAT nodes), *adjust GeoDNS fallback rules for maintenance windows*, and *teach batch API to respect region pin at create-time*.
Wei: also add a probe that marks a region degraded when token_exchange or gpu-allocation latency spikes (not only LB probe). That would avoid routing away from origin when we still have pinned workloads.
Lucas: agreed. putting a ticket: INFRA-5203 "SNAT autoscale + enhanced region health probe" — I'll include runbook updates.
Maya: quick check: can someone verify conntrack counts on the us-west1 NAT nodes?
Jamal: grabbing now: `ssh nat-gw-03` -> `sudo conntrack -S | grep tcp` shows ~62k entries, ephemeral port usage near 65500.
Maya: ugh. we were dangerously close.
oncall-bot: escalation: paging infra oncall (rotation) — please join #incident-2009999999 for coordination
Sara: I'll own the postmortem and cost calc. tagging @finance for chargeback.
Maya: thanks all — monitoring shows jobs requeued and success rate climbing back to normal at 08:45 UTC. leaving this thread open for action item tracking. :thumbsup:
